90:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Balad In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful This is an oath from God, the Blessed and Exalted, by Makkah, the Mother of Cities, when its inhabitants are in a state of ihram, to draw attention to its great status when its people are in a state of ihram. Khasif said on the authority of Mujahid, I swear by this city, not to refute them. I swear by this city. Shabib ibn Bishr said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, I swear by this city, meaning Makkah, and you are a resident of this city, meaning you, O Muhammad, it is permissible for you to encounter it. This is also narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Abu Salih, Atiyyah, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd. Mujahid said, Whatever you acquire there is permissible for you. Qatadah said, and you are a resident of this city, meaning you are in it without any difficulty or sin. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, God made it permissible for him for an hour of the day. This is the meaning that they said, and the hadith that is agreed upon to be authentic is also narrated in it. “This country was made sacred by God on the day He created the heavens and the earth. It is sacred by God’s sanctity until the Day of Resurrection. No one may cut its trees or seclude themselves in it. It was only made lawful for me for one hour of a day, and today its sanctity has returned to what it was yesterday. So let the witness inform the absent.” And in another version: If someone seeks permission to fight the Messenger of God, then say that God gave permission to His Messenger but did not give you permission. God the Almighty said: And a father and that which he begot. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ibn Atiyyah told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding God the Almighty’s saying: And a father and that which he begot, the father who gives birth and that which he begot, the barren woman who has no children. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Sharik, who is Ibn Abdullah, the judge. Ikrimah said: the barren father and that which he begot, the one who gives birth. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Mujahid, Abu Salih, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Sufyan Ath-Thawri, Sa’id ibn Hubayr, As-Suddi, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Khasif, Shurahbil ibn Sa’d and others said: By father he means Adam and that which his son begot. This view of Mujahid and his companions is good and strong, because when God the Almighty swore by the Mother of Cities, which is the mother of dwellings, He swore after that by the inhabitant, which is Adam, the father of mankind, and his son. Abu Imran Al-Jawni said: It is Abraham and his offspring. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir preferred that it is general for every father and his son, and it is also open to interpretation. And the saying of God the Almighty: Indeed, We created man in toil was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, Ibn `Abbas, `Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ibrahim al-Nakha`i, Khaithamah, al-Dahhak, and others, meaning upright. Ibn `Abbas added in a narration on his authority: upright in his mother’s womb. The liver is straightness and uprightness. The meaning of this statement is that We created him straight and upright, like the saying of God the Almighty: O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? Who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you? In whatever form He willed has He assembled you? And like the saying of God the Almighty: Indeed, We created man in the best stature. Ibn Abi Najih, Jurayj, and `Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: In toil means in the severity of creation. Have you not seen him? And he mentioned his birth and the emergence of his teeth. Mujahid said: In toil means a sperm, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, he struggles with creation. Mujahid said: It is like the saying of God the Almighty: His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and she breastfed him with hardship and his livelihood was with hardship, so he struggles with that. Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: Indeed, We created man in toil Liver in hardship and seeking his livelihood. Ikrimah said: in hardship and length. Qatada said: in difficulty. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Issam told us, Abu Asim told us, Abdul Hamid bin Jaafar told us, I heard Muhammad bin Ali Abu Jaafar al-Baqir ask a man from the Ansar about the statement of God the Most High: Indeed We created man into hardship. He said: in his standing and uprightness. Abu Jaafar did not object to him. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Mawdud that I heard al-Hasan recite this verse: Indeed We created man into hardship. He said: he struggles with a matter of this world and a matter of the Hereafter. In another narration: he struggles with the hardships of this world and the hardships of the Hereafter. Ibn Zayd said: Indeed We created man into hardship. He said: Adam was created in the heaven and that was called the liver. Ibn Jarir chose that what is meant by that is struggling with matters and their difficulties. God the Almighty says: {Does he think that no one has power over him?} Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: meaning, Does he think that no one has power over him takes his money. Qatadah said: {Does he think that no one has power over him?” He said: The son of Adam thinks that he will not be asked about this money, how he acquired it, and where he spent it. Al-Suddi said: {Does he think that no one has power over him?} God the Almighty said: {He will say, I have spent wealth in abundance.} meaning, the son of Adam says, I have spent wealth in abundance, meaning, a lot. This was said by Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, and others. {Does He think that no one sees him?”} Mujahid said: meaning, does he think that God the Almighty does not see him? Others among the early Muslims said the same. God the Almighty says: {Have We not made for him two eyes?” meaning with them he sees. And a tongue meaning with which he speaks, expressing what is in his mind. And two lips meaning with which he speaks, to help him speak, eat food, and to beautify his face and mouth. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Abu al-Rabi’ al-Dimashqi on the authority of Makhul who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty says: O son of Adam, I have bestowed upon you great blessings, the number of which you cannot count nor be able to thank for. Among the blessings I have bestowed upon you is that I have given you two eyes with which to look and have given them coverings. So look with your eyes at what I have made lawful for you, and if you see what I have forbidden, close their coverings. I have given you a tongue and given it a covering, so speak what I have commanded you and made lawful for you. If what I have forbidden is presented to you, then close your tongue. I have given you a vagina and a veil, so offer with your vagina what I have made lawful for you, and if what I have forbidden is presented to you, then let down your veil. O son of Adam, you cannot bear My wrath nor can bear My vengeance.” And We showed him the two Najds the two paths. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas`ud. And We showed him the two Najds he said: good and evil. This is how it was narrated on the authority of Ali, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Abu Wa'il, Abu Salih, Muhammad Ibn Ka`b, al-Dahhak, and Ata' al-Khurasani, among others. Abdullah Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Lahi`ah informed me on the authority of Yazid Ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Sinan Ibn Sa`d, on the authority of Anas Ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are two Najds, and the evil Najd has not been made more beloved to you than the good Najd. Ahmad said: I abandoned his hadith due to his confusion. He narrated fifteen fabricated hadiths, all of which I do not know of a single hadith that resembles his hadith, the hadith of al-Hasan - meaning al-Basri - but does not resemble the hadith of Anas. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, who said: I heard Al-Hasan say: And We showed him the two highlands. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “O people, indeed the two highlands are Najd al-Khair and Najd al-Shar. So what has been made Najd al-Shar is more beloved to you than Najd al-Khair.” And this is how Habib bin Al-Shaheed, Muammar, Yunus bin Ubayd, and Abu Wahb narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan, without a chain of transmission. And this is how Qatada narrated it without a chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Issam Al-Ansari told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Isa bin Affan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: And We showed him the two highlands, he said: The two breasts. And something similar was narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Khathim, Qatadah, and Abu Hazim. And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Isa bin Uqal, with this chain of transmission. Then he said: The correct statement is the first one, and similar to this verse is the words of God the Almighty: “Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture that We may try him; and We made him hearing and seeing. Indeed, We guided him to the way, whether he be grateful.” Or ungrateful.

Ka’b al-Ahbar said: And he did not storm the steep path means seventy degrees in Hell. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: And he did not storm the steep path meaning a steep path in Hell. Qatada said: It is a steep steep path, so storm it in obedience to God Almighty. Qatada said: And what will make you know what the ‘Aqaba is? Then God the Almighty informed about storming it, saying: The freeing of a slave * Or feeding. Ibn Zayd said: Then why did he storm the ‘Aqaba? That is, why did he not take the path that leads to salvation and goodness? Then between them, God the Almighty said: And what will make you know what the ‘Aqaba is? The freeing of a slave * Or feeding. The ‘freeing of a slave’ was read as an addition, and it was read as a verb with the subject pronoun and the slave as its object, and both readings have similar meanings. Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Ibrahim told us, Abdullah - meaning ibn Sa’id ibn Abi Hind - told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Hakeem, the client of the family of Az-Zubayr, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Marjana that he heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever frees a believing slave, God will free for every limb of hers a limb of his from the Fire, so that he frees a hand, a foot, and a vagina. Ali ibn al-Husayn said: Did you hear this from Abu Hurayrah? Saeed said: Yes. Then Ali ibn al-Husayn said to his servant, the most knowledgeable of his servants: Call Mutarrif. When he stood in front of him, he said: Go, you are free for the sake of God. It was narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i through various chains of narration on the authority of Saeed ibn Marjana. Muslim has it that this servant, whom Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin had freed, had been given ten thousand dirhams for him. This Abu Nujayh is ‘Umar ibn ‘Abasah al-Sulami may God be pleased with him.
